<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36059">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.36059-mnemon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f832a1b58f4143d5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mnemon" data-paper-title="Mnemon: Raw Records, Fast Judgments, Slow Thoughts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-42c0610048928da3">Why separate slow search planning from fast record decisions instead of reasoning at length about every record?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amnemon">Mnemon: Raw Records, Fast Judgments, Slow Thoughts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Planning chooses where to seek evidence; per-record eligibility fits a bounded fast decision. Separation spends reasoning budget on search direction rather than repeatedly explaining candidates. Dated originals remain, while the answerer sees a small budgeted view. Fast decisions do not guarantee complete evidence or correct time eligibility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Decide to search a release meeting, quickly screen dozens of records, then send a few originals to the answerer instead of analyzing every record at length.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36059">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.36059-mnemon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-42c0610048928da3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mnemon" data-paper-title="Mnemon: Raw Records, Fast Judgments, Slow Thoughts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1831a12ab0dad173">How do dated raw records compare with repeatedly rewriting one long-term summary for traceability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amnemon">Mnemon: Raw Records, Fast Judgments, Slow Thoughts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Raw records retain exact wording, time, and details for different questions, but cost storage and query-time reading. A rolling summary is compact yet can erase provenance or rare facts. Mnemon builds a budgeted view from originals for this query, not a permanent lossless replacement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A summary says the customer prefers A, while the dated email says only this quarter. Check the original before answering about next quarter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36059">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.36059-mnemon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1831a12ab0dad173">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:mnemon" data-paper-title="Mnemon: Raw Records, Fast Judgments, Slow Thoughts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-421fc3dc6770c6a3">Does the local bounded-view test cover Jev semantic judgments and the original answer model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amnemon">Mnemon: Raw Records, Fast Judgments, Slow Thoughts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It runs raw-record retrieval and budgeted view construction without a Jev checkpoint or reproducing LoCoMo scores. Record order, dates, and budget are independently checkable. Real models are needed to test semantic necessity and whether the answerer uses evidence correctly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Fitting three specified records verifies the view interface, not that the judge selects them from natural language.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36059">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.36059-mnemon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-421fc3dc6770c6a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ccm" data-paper-title="Continuous Context Management" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-ccm-d42ba3fe" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6254981077290624">What kind of context growth is CCM trying to avoid across many turns?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Accm">Continuous Context Management</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Miami</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Resending every observation, action, and thought grows cumulative input and can bury current state. CCM lets the agent maintain bounded memory each turn and keep acting. It studies how to compress the past into decision-sufficient state rather than retain complete history indefinitely.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: At step ninety, current files, verified results, and pending work may suffice without every terminal output from the previous 89 steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35540">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.35540-ccm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6254981077290624">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ccm" data-paper-title="Continuous Context Management" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2ae6086f325e6ed3">If the training teacher sees full history, why can the next student turn see only bounded memory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Accm">Continuous Context Management</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Miami</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Privileged history supplies training signals, while the deployed student still sees the task, memory, and latest observation. This forces it to write necessary state into limited space. Providing full history at evaluation bypasses continuous management. Memory updates accompany actions and must serve the next decision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A teacher knows a port number mentioned earlier. The student must preserve it in small memory rather than receive the whole earlier conversation on test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35540">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.35540-ccm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2ae6086f325e6ed3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ccm" data-paper-title="Continuous Context Management" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-70af81e05a5b670f">How does per-turn bounded state differ from retrieving a few old records just before answering?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Accm">Continuous Context Management</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Miami</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>CCM updates memory during each action, so retention now determines next-turn visibility. Answer-time retrieval makes the main selection later using an external index. The bottlenecks differ and can complement each other. Bounded-state omissions cannot rely on hidden history, and retrieval must count indexing and reads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A terminal changes directories. CCM should immediately keep the path; later retrieving an old command alone may miss the directory change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35540">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.35540-ccm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-70af81e05a5b670f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ccm" data-paper-title="Continuous Context Management" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7faceb47315133fb">How do you check that CCM does not bypass bounded context with unrecorded history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Accm">Continuous Context Management</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Miami</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Inspect that each policy request contains only the original task, current memory, and latest observation. Prior tool results are visible only if written into memory, which has a hard cap. The local run tests these contracts without TerminalBench or WebShop checkpoints; field isolation is not task capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Hiding a full previous transcript in an extra metadata field violates the contract even if the main prompt is shorter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35540">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.35540-ccm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7faceb47315133fb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:interactive-memory" data-paper-title="Interactive Memory Learning for Long-Term Conversations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-interactive-memory-e350b33d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-705ddd2a1311bf6e">Why is it hard for a cross-session assistant to know on day one what will matter on day three?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ainteractive-memory">Interactive Memory Learning for Long-Term Conversations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen / Pengcheng Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Future requests have not occurred. The writer chooses likely durable facts from observed conversation, and the reader retrieves them in suitable contexts. Interactive Memory learns from actual future usefulness rather than giving the writer future questions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A user casually mentions avoiding peanuts on day one and asks for meal planning on day three. The value of that note becomes evident later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17088">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.17088-interactive-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-705ddd2a1311bf6e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:interactive-memory" data-paper-title="Interactive Memory Learning for Long-Term Conversations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e0579dd9a1ccc407">Why jointly learn a write Planner and read Trigger from delayed cross-session reward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ainteractive-memory">Interactive Memory Learning for Long-Term Conversations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen / Pengcheng Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Some details reveal their usefulness only in later sessions. Retrieval timing determines whether they affect results. Shared delayed reward links writing to later use instead of rewarding summary quality alone. Evaluate in chronological order; future questions must not preselect what to write.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Saving a changed workplace matters for commute planning next week. Same-day chat fluency may never reward saving it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17088">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.17088-interactive-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e0579dd9a1ccc407">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:interactive-memory" data-paper-title="Interactive Memory Learning for Long-Term Conversations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-90095b41840d15b6">How does delayed cross-session reward differ from reward based on per-turn retrieval similarity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ainteractive-memory">Interactive Memory Learning for Long-Term Conversations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen / Pengcheng Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similarity is an immediate proxy that may not predict later use. Delayed reward observes later dialogue outcomes to learn long-term writing and trigger value. It introduces credit assignment; revealing future questions to the writer would no longer test learning for an unknown future.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An allergy detail may be unrelated to the present topic yet crucial for ordering later. Similarity can underestimate that long-term value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17088">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.17088-interactive-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-90095b41840d15b6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:interactive-memory" data-paper-title="Interactive Memory Learning for Long-Term Conversations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-210029a079c17858">Why distinguish information available at writing time from later evaluation in an observation-safe state machine?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ainteractive-memory">Interactive Memory Learning for Long-Term Conversations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen / Pengcheng Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The writer sees observations available then. Future questions, answers, and scores can supply external reward only after the corresponding execution. Local Planner/Trigger diagnostics verify isolation and feedback, not paper-scale training or learned preferences from preset fixture rewards.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Hiding day three&#x27;s question in day one&#x27;s write input makes fact selection easy, but this lookahead leak invalidates the learning claim.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与实现对应, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17088">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.17088-interactive-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-210029a079c17858">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evoskill-gui" data-paper-title="Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-evoskill-gui-aeb4c952" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-37640d1b810cdf3f">Why can GUI skills become invalid as interfaces and tasks change?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevoskill-gui">Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Button positions, page sequence, and preconditions can change. A skill that worked before need not execute in a new state. EvoSkill-GUI studies converting observed failures into verified improvements for later reuse. Training-free still requires real observations and execution checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A top-right button moves into a menu. Replaying the old trace fails, so revise the corresponding step from the current screen.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17653">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.17653-evoskill-gui/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-37640d1b810cdf3f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evoskill-gui" data-paper-title="Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2dd3ecf51946e14e">Why is changing only the responsible GUI skill component more auditable than regenerating the whole skill?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevoskill-gui">Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A local edit ties failure evidence to one component and preserves other verified behaviors. This makes it easier to tell whether the patch fixed the defect without broad drift. A critic needs information isolation, not hidden answers. Verify the revised skill before reusing it elsewhere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If login fails only when closing a pop-up, first fix that locator rather than rewrite username entry and submission too.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17653">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.17653-evoskill-gui/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2dd3ecf51946e14e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evoskill-gui" data-paper-title="Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a807ac97630fd951">How does local revision by an isolated critic differ from ad hoc self-editing by the executor?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevoskill-gui">Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The critic independently attributes failure from permitted evidence, limits patch scope, and verifies before reuse. Ad hoc edits can carry over the executor&#x27;s wrong assumptions. Isolation controls evidence and responsibility rather than guaranteeing correctness; retain failure evidence and validation results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The executor assumes a page finished loading. A critic can identify a missing wait from observations instead of accepting that the button is absent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17653">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.17653-evoskill-gui/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a807ac97630fd951">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:evoskill-gui" data-paper-title="Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8dc3dffbfabb507d">Can the local public-observation patch demo establish cross-task reuse on real GUIs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aevoskill-gui">Reflect, Revise, Reuse: Training-Free Skill Evolution for GUI Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It reads public evidence and applies bounded reference edits without MobileWorld, AndroidWorld, or OSWorld. It verifies no gold access, patch scope, and state transitions. Real screen understanding, clicking, and validated cross-task success remain unestablished.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Updating a locator after a button name changes in a string verifies the patch contract, not finding that button in an actual screenshot.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17653">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.17653-evoskill-gui/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8dc3dffbfabb507d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skill-retention" data-paper-title="When Synthetic Data Hurts: On Catastrophic Forgetting in Skill Retrieval for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-skill-retention-6ccb63cf" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c8463c103cf3df10">Why evaluate both new skills and existing user needs when training skill retrieval?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askill-retention">When Synthetic Data Hurts: On Catastrophic Forgetting in Skill Retrieval for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Manulife</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>New data adapts the retriever to a larger skill catalog, but service still receives familiar real and out-of-domain queries. The goal is retaining old routing while learning new material, not only minimizing loss on new data. Improvements on new tasks do not erase the cost of forgetting existing usage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A model works on synthetic examples with canonical function names, but users still describe their needs colloquially. Those queries are not obsolete.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10750">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.10750-skill-retention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c8463c103cf3df10">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skill-retention" data-paper-title="When Synthetic Data Hurts: On Catastrophic Forgetting in Skill Retrieval for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b9b020e8d70e745d">Why might more synthetic skill data hurt retrieval on real tasks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askill-retention">When Synthetic Data Hurts: On Catastrophic Forgetting in Skill Retrieval for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Manulife</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Synthetic language and distributions can differ from real requests, shifting embeddings and routing boundaries toward synthetic patterns. Replay preserves real task coverage; anchoring or distillation from an old model limits drift. These protect transfer and retention, not a guarantee that more synthetic data helps or forgetting disappears.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Synthetic requests always spell out tool names, while real users use abbreviations. Training only on synthetic wording may miss real requests; replaying abbreviations preserves old routing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10750">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.10750-skill-retention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b9b020e8d70e745d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skill-retention" data-paper-title="When Synthetic Data Hurts: On Catastrophic Forgetting in Skill Retrieval for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-80ec601077b5e3e4">What do real-data replay and embedding anchors or LwF constrain differently?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askill-retention">When Synthetic Data Hurts: On Catastrophic Forgetting in Skill Retrieval for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Manulife</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Replay exposes optimization to old tasks; anchors or Learning without Forgetting limit representation or output drift. One provides data coverage and the other constrains behavioral changes induced by updates. They are complementary, not redundant. Too much weight can inhibit new skill learning, so validate the trade-off.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Replay old colloquial requests and separately constrain their embeddings not to move far. That protects old retrieval through both examples and representation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10750">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.10750-skill-retention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-80ec601077b5e3e4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skill-retention" data-paper-title="When Synthetic Data Hurts: On Catastrophic Forgetting in Skill Retrieval for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a1783c4ed93b7227">Does passing local anchor, conflict penalty, and replay checks include training the 0.6B retriever?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askill-retention">When Synthetic Data Hurts: On Catastrophic Forgetting in Skill Retrieval for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Manulife</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The local reference runs route anchors and associated constraints without training the 0.6B model over more than thirty thousand skills. It checks replay participation, anchor-loss direction, and conflict handling. Synthetic state changes do not establish real or OOD retrieval retention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Pulling one vector toward its old anchor verifies the gradient, not correct skill retrieval for unseen wording.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式或操作, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10750">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.10750-skill-retention/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a1783c4ed93b7227">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:grounded-memory" data-paper-title="Grounding Agent Memory: Environment-Probing Curation for Enterprise Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-grounded-memory-32bdf0be" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-987d0970e9c03a33">Why can&#x27;t an enterprise agent treat a guess after one execution as long-term knowledge?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agrounded-memory">Grounding Agent Memory: Environment-Probing Curation for Enterprise Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Permissions, configuration, and interfaces change, and one failure may be temporary. Grounded Memory requires traceable environmental evidence and a scope before persisting experience. Recording what happened is only part of knowing where and when it holds.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A repository access failure today does not mean the service is permanently unavailable. A durable conclusion needs clearer state evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11060">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.11060-grounded-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-987d0970e9c03a33">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:grounded-memory" data-paper-title="Grounding Agent Memory: Environment-Probing Curation for Enterprise Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b73212381aeefde5">Why should a memory curator probe the environment with least-privilege read-only tools before writing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agrounded-memory">Grounding Agent Memory: Environment-Probing Curation for Enterprise Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Conversation claims may be stale or environment-specific. Probing ties candidate memory to current observable facts and scope. Read-only least privilege avoids changing the observed system. A verified claim holds under those conditions, not permanently or everywhere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A claim that the server runs on port eight thousand can be checked in read-only configuration and scoped to that environment. Do not edit the config to make it true.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11060">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.11060-grounded-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b73212381aeefde5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:grounded-memory" data-paper-title="Grounding Agent Memory: Environment-Probing Curation for Enterprise Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e27661bed1b5020f">How does admission by environment probing differ from direct LLM summarization of experience?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agrounded-memory">Grounding Agent Memory: Environment-Probing Curation for Enterprise Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Summarization relies on trace text and can turn guesses into facts. Independent probes can reject contradictions and narrow scope, but add query and maintenance cost and can verify only observable conditions. A verification step does not make every enterprise state reliable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A missing path in one repository should not become a claim about all projects. A probe can scope it to the current repository and revision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11060">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.11060-grounded-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e27661bed1b5020f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:grounded-memory" data-paper-title="Grounding Agent Memory: Environment-Probing Curation for Enterprise Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-84beb1f3d4030a3e">Why must a curator not turn a least-privilege read-only tool into a repair action?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agrounded-memory">Grounding Agent Memory: Environment-Probing Curation for Enterprise Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The curator verifies candidate memory. Writing changes the state it is trying to observe and introduces side effects. Local tests cover repeated probing, conflict rejection, and admission, not Copilot SDK integration. Passing call contracts does not reproduce enterprise agent costs or outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If a value differs, update the memory&#x27;s evidence rather than editing live configuration back to the old value and calling the old memory verified.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式或操作, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11060">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.11060-grounded-memory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-84beb1f3d4030a3e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memforest" data-paper-title="MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-memforest-6306606d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7faeaf7a8b79a728">Why must long-term memory support both an overview and a return to specific events?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemforest">MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reading all raw history costs too much, but a single summary can omit the source of a decision. MemForest keeps events locally structured and progressively compresses under capacity pressure while preserving paths back to evidence. It balances scale with traceable detail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Finding which meeting changed a plan last month requires both its event cluster and the actual confirmation message.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08273">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.08273-memforest/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7faeaf7a8b79a728">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memforest" data-paper-title="MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f36339169a34d4f1">Why do progressively merged event trees help locate evidence better than repeatedly rewriting a global summary under pressure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemforest">MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Event partitions preserve local time and causal structure. Merge only necessary nodes rather than disturbing all history. Queries propagate from semantic anchors through neighborhood links, including cross-event relations. Hierarchical summaries can still lose details; trees control loss and lookup paths without guaranteeing losslessness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A failed payment and later refund are separate events linked across trees. Rewriting one global summary may blur their order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08273">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.08273-memforest/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f36339169a34d4f1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memforest" data-paper-title="MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-202f62121d392bce">How does semantic-anchor neighborhood propagation differ from retrieving only the most similar node?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemforest">MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A single match may be superficially related. Propagation can add context via temporal and cross-event links. This structure expands evidence but can also add noise, so control propagation range and budget. Neighboring nodes are not automatically correct evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: After matching a rescheduling proposal, read the neighboring confirmation to learn whether the new date took effect.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08273">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.08273-memforest/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-202f62121d392bce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memforest" data-paper-title="MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ff77fee8acfdac1a">Where does the local token-Jaccard EventTree stop short of the paper&#x27;s embeddings and LLM summarizer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemforest">MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shanghai Jiao Tong University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local CPU structures select trees by term Jaccard and run compression, checking partitioning and merging. They do not run author embeddings, an LLM summarizer, or long-horizon benchmarks. Structural correctness and fewer records do not establish semantic retrieval or QA capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two nodes sharing meeting can match by Jaccard. Whether they describe the same event requires richer semantics not proved by this interface.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08273">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.08273-memforest/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ff77fee8acfdac1a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coskill" data-paper-title="CoSkill: Joint Reinforcement Learning of Reasoning and Meta-Skill Agents for Hierarchical Skill Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-coskill-9fe84c48" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bc25b0a6a77ac396">Why is CoSkill&#x27;s Meta-Skill Agent a learnable policy rather than a fixed script?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoskill">CoSkill: Joint Reinforcement Learning of Reasoning and Meta-Skill Agents for Hierarchical Skill Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It edits skill contents based on execution returns. The Reasoning Agent learns to select and use task and substep skills. Roles share a backbone and update alternately, adapting the library and action policy together. Verify that edits improve actual execution before keeping them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: When the reasoning role finds a missing recovery step, Meta-Skill proposes a change and validates after resetting the environment instead of permanently saving every reflection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04865">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.04865-coskill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bc25b0a6a77ac396">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coskill" data-paper-title="CoSkill: Joint Reinforcement Learning of Reasoning and Meta-Skill Agents for Hierarchical Skill Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4f7ee74d56713c41">Why can shared team reward adapt both the reasoning and Meta-Skill policies?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoskill">CoSkill: Joint Reinforcement Learning of Reasoning and Meta-Skill Agents for Hierarchical Skill Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Skill content determines available procedures, and reasoning choices determine which skills get execution feedback. A joint objective connects both to task results; alternating updates reduces the risk of a revised library being unused or a revised policy being limited by old skills. Shared reward does not solve credit assignment for each edit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If a long skill fails, Meta-Skill can shorten it while the reasoning agent learns when to invoke the revision instead of merely storing a new document.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04865">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.04865-coskill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4f7ee74d56713c41">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coskill" data-paper-title="CoSkill: Joint Reinforcement Learning of Reasoning and Meta-Skill Agents for Hierarchical Skill Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-343636ce44e2ae97">How does joint training differ from training retrieval over a fixed skill library?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoskill">CoSkill: Joint Reinforcement Learning of Reasoning and Meta-Skill Agents for Hierarchical Skill Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed library changes only what is selected. Joint training also changes skill contents that may not suit the task, increasing nonstationarity and attribution difficulty. Role credit, isolated edits, and rejecting non-improving updates matter; library growth does not imply stronger teamwork.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Better retrieval cannot fix steps in the wrong order. Meta-Skill can fix the order, but must check other tasks for regressions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04865">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.04865-coskill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-343636ce44e2ae97">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coskill" data-paper-title="CoSkill: Joint Reinforcement Learning of Reasoning and Meta-Skill Agents for Hierarchical Skill Evolution" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f303b868421584ec">How should actual updates across three local seeds without promotion be interpreted?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoskill">CoSkill: Joint Reinforcement Learning of Reasoning and Meta-Skill Agents for Hierarchical Skill Evolution</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both roles had nonzero gradients and parameter changes, but reset validation showed no positive gain. The skill candidate was not promoted and the baseline champion stayed. Old results that read evaluation labels are void, and legacy parsing is not capability. Local Qwen ToolRoute is not comparable with paper ALFWorld/WebShop scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Large parameter movement without validation gain proves execution and rejection work, not that CoSkill improves success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04865">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.04865-coskill/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f303b868421584ec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:atomrec" data-paper-title="AtomRec: Evolving Atomic Memory for Agentic Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-atomrec-2a7b7ab5" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-351629bdd8e2893b">Why does a recommendation assistant need user memory that tracks changes and evidence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aatomrec">AtomRec: Evolving Atomic Memory for Agentic Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xi&#x27;an Jiaotong-Liverpool University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Behavior reflects long-term preferences, short-term intent, and item-specific feedback. A fixed profile is hard to update or explain. AtomRec evolves evidence at a fine granularity and uses history relations to explain candidates. A single click need not imply long-term preference, so retain context and provenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A gift perfume purchase should not make the system infer that the user personally prefers that scent long term.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04882">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.04882-atomrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-351629bdd8e2893b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:atomrec" data-paper-title="AtomRec: Evolving Atomic Memory for Agentic Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8309c3740cf37d71">Why does an atomic user profile help keep new preferences from overwriting old ones?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aatomrec">AtomRec: Evolving Atomic Memory for Agentic Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xi&#x27;an Jiaotong-Liverpool University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Updates touch matching fact fields without rewriting the whole profile, reducing incidental deletions or semantic drift. Semantic collaborative edges and multi-hop paths connect recommendation evidence separately from preference values. Atomic fields still require conflict and time handling; old facts are not automatically permanent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A new no-spicy-dinner preference changes that field only, preserving commute budget and breakfast preferences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04882">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.04882-atomrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8309c3740cf37d71">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:atomrec" data-paper-title="AtomRec: Evolving Atomic Memory for Agentic Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7726f178d983b0c6">How does a multi-hop evidence path differ from one collaborative user–item edge?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aatomrec">AtomRec: Evolving Atomic Memory for Agentic Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xi&#x27;an Jiaotong-Liverpool University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A direct edge gives overall association. A multi-hop path can trace preference through a historical item attribute to a candidate. Semantic edges may still be wrong, so reachability is not causal proof of preference. Evaluate downstream ranking on a closed candidate set with target isolation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Linking the lightweight attribute of previously liked shoes to a new pair is more traceable than saying they are often bought together, if the attribute link is grounded in actual history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04882">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.04882-atomrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7726f178d983b0c6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:atomrec" data-paper-title="AtomRec: Evolving Atomic Memory for Agentic Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-781bdb947b2bb38f">What do local pre-target reconstruction and zeroing illegal links prevent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aatomrec">AtomRec: Evolving Atomic Memory for Agentic Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xi&#x27;an Jiaotong-Liverpool University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rebuild memory from history strictly before each held-out target to prevent future behavior leakage. Generated links can cite only provided historical IDs; malformed or illegal output fails without reference-answer backfill. The small local test is negative, so executed data flow is not a recommendation or online gain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Seeing the target product in later history makes the task easier. Remove it in the time-correct reconstruction, not just hide the prompt field name.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04882">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.04882-atomrec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-781bdb947b2bb38f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skilldreamer" data-paper-title="Imagine Before Acting: Prospective Skill Identification for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-skilldreamer-d1e698b9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1051cd50b705bb42">Why is a pseudo skill a retrieval proxy rather than a verified procedure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askilldreamer">Imagine Before Acting: Prospective Skill Identification for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sichuan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The model imagines capabilities and procedure-like descriptions to bridge task wording and skill documents. These descriptions have not been executed and may omit steps or violate conditions. Load and validate the real procedure before acting; a complete-looking description is not proof.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A pseudo skill says export and verify files in bulk. It helps find the export skill, but real parameters, permissions, and checks come from the actual documentation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01642">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.01642-skilldreamer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1051cd50b705bb42">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skilldreamer" data-paper-title="Imagine Before Acting: Prospective Skill Identification for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-874ddf7bcc58f94f">After generating a pseudo skill, why does CSI recheck capability fit before execution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askilldreamer">Imagine Before Acting: Prospective Skill Identification for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sichuan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The pseudo skill turns a goal into a procedural retrieval proxy. It may locate related documents, but it is not verified and may not fit the subgoal. CSI rechecks evidence, constraints, and the next bounded action, linking retrieval to correct use without assuming imagined steps are executable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A pseudo skill can find a web download procedure. Before executing, check whether the current page requires login instead of following a similar document title blindly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01642">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.01642-skilldreamer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-874ddf7bcc58f94f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skilldreamer" data-paper-title="Imagine Before Acting: Prospective Skill Identification for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f40d500470486920">What is HSR capability round-robin trading off against global top-score selection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askilldreamer">Imagine Before Acting: Prospective Skill Identification for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sichuan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Global top scores can all come from one easily matched capability, missing other requirements. HSR ranks within capability and cycles through rows with deduplication to preserve coverage. Min–max normalization within candidate sets makes scores set-dependent, not calibrated success probabilities across tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A task needs cleaning, plotting, and export. Round-robin gives each a candidate instead of using all five slots for cleaning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01642">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.01642-skilldreamer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f40d500470486920">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skilldreamer" data-paper-title="Imagine Before Acting: Prospective Skill Identification for LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9583328c6cf5170b">Does CSI check every five reasoning turns or every five executed actions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askilldreamer">Imagine Before Acting: Prospective Skill Identification for LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sichuan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It counts actually executed actions. Before the next action, recheck the current subgoal, evidence, and constraints; MATCH or PARTIAL_MATCH loads the real procedure first. Loading is not tool success, and invalid pseudo skills are not heuristically fabricated. Report loads, executions, and final passes separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Three reflections without tool execution do not advance the action counter or trigger the periodic check early.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 数据协议、结果与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01642">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.01642-skilldreamer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9583328c6cf5170b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:spt" data-paper-title="SPT: Skills as Pre-Training Data for Agentic Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-spt-bfd17eb8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c27cd9a103e2836c">Why can multi-file skill packages serve as mid-training data for a causal LM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspt">SPT: Skills as Pre-Training Data for Agentic Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They contain reusable procedures and referenced materials. Predicting this text before post-training can build workflow priors. This is not a single execution trace or real tool use during training; downstream SFT or RL still must turn document patterns into behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Instructions with a configuration example and helper script teach a reusable method, not the accidental full tool log of one task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26563">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.26563-spt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c27cd9a103e2836c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:spt" data-paper-title="SPT: Skills as Pre-Training Data for Agentic Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-40ec6a0c367caa76">Why is inserting referenced files near first use more complete than pretraining on skill instructions alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspt">SPT: Skills as Pre-Training Data for Agentic Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications</p>
