<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Skill packages put argument rules or examples in companion files. Inlining at first reference exposes real dependencies at the right position in causal context rather than training on dangling references. Mixing with general text limits distribution shift. Reading skill documents is not validated execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: &#x27;Use schema.json for arguments&#x27; does not teach the field constraints if the schema is absent; inserting it near the reference supplies them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26563">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.26563-spt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-40ec6a0c367caa76">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:spt" data-paper-title="SPT: Skills as Pre-Training Data for Agentic Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a101e15d0ef1c12a">How does skill mid-training differ from retrieving skill documents only at deployment?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspt">SPT: Skills as Pre-Training Data for Agentic Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Mid-training writes procedural patterns into weights, so the same document need not be retrieved each time. Runtime retrieval puts up-to-date skills explicitly in context but costs tokens. They can complement each other. Training on skill text does not prove tool execution; verify a real policy and environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A model may remember to verify before submitting, while a changed API argument still needs current runtime documentation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26563">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.26563-spt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a101e15d0ef1c12a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:spt" data-paper-title="SPT: Skills as Pre-Training Data for Agentic Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ca6f583af366bb98">Why retain general text and control its mixture with skill data in mid-training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aspt">SPT: Skills as Pre-Training Data for Agentic Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Training data changes both what a model learns and the text distribution it sees. An explicit mixture coefficient α controls the share of procedural packages. Replacing all training with skill documents does not leave other capabilities unchanged by assumption. Local assembly and mixture tests cannot establish general capability retention or execution skill.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A batch includes instructions and general prose. Raising the skill ratio changes the training emphasis, which requires training evaluation, not a file-count check.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26563">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.26563-spt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ca6f583af366bb98">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:covemem" data-paper-title="When Memory Takes Gradients: Collaborative Vector Memory for Agentic Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-covemem-d06a5714" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-44e841fd1f10ce70">Why does CoVeMem retrieve collaborative memory based on the current candidate set?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acovemem">When Memory Takes Gradients: Collaborative Vector Memory for Agentic Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shenzhen Technology University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The average collaborative candidate representation describes the local need. The system retrieves matching history and projects it into LLM-readable soft tokens. This focuses memory on the ranking task rather than a fixed text profile of all history. New candidates can change retrieval for the same user.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Outdoor-gear candidates may retrieve related purchases, while skin-care candidates retrieve a different portion of the same user&#x27;s history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26895">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.26895-covemem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-44e841fd1f10ce70">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:covemem" data-paper-title="When Memory Takes Gradients: Collaborative Vector Memory for Agentic Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d1a6536e3ba1db6b">Why use semantic alignment and a masked listwise objective instead of simply making LightGCN vectors soft tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acovemem">When Memory Takes Gradients: Collaborative Vector Memory for Agentic Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shenzhen Technology University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Matching projection dimension does not ensure use of collaborative geometry. Semantic alignment constrains the interface, and within-candidate ranking forces relevant memory to affect predictions. Candidate-driven retrieval changes history by option set. A frozen bank does not remove connector training or make explanations inherently faithful.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The same user needs different history for movies and books. Ranking supervision must teach soft tokens to affect the corresponding candidate scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26895">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.26895-covemem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d1a6536e3ba1db6b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:covemem" data-paper-title="When Memory Takes Gradients: Collaborative Vector Memory for Agentic Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-78cbec70ede61b68">How does collaborative soft-token memory differ from repeatedly rewriting a textual profile?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acovemem">When Memory Takes Gradients: Collaborative Vector Memory for Agentic Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shenzhen Technology University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Soft tokens preserve collaborative geometry from a frozen LightGCN bank and use projection and alignment to interface with an LM. Text profiles are readable but require generative rewrites and can lose catalog structure. Vector interfaces need training and interpretation limits. No extra text-maintenance calls does not mean zero inference cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Ranking can read collaborative vectors without asking an LLM to rewrite preferences, but projection, retrieval, and language forward passes still consume compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26895">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.26895-covemem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-78cbec70ede61b68">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:covemem" data-paper-title="When Memory Takes Gradients: Collaborative Vector Memory for Agentic Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-276bc00150e629ff">How does the mean candidate vector choose which collaborative memories to read from user history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acovemem">When Memory Takes Gradients: Collaborative Vector Memory for Agentic Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shenzhen Technology University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Average the current candidates&#x27; vectors in the frozen bank, score historical items against that mean, select relevant items, and project them for the LLM. Changing candidates can change the read even when history is fixed. The local run verifies conditional retrieval, not training the paper&#x27;s LightGCN, connector, or LoRA.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Switching the candidate set from cameras to hiking boots changes the mean and can surface photography versus outdoor interactions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26895">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.26895-covemem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-276bc00150e629ff">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skill-state" data-paper-title="SKILL.state: Scalable Long-Horizon Agent Skills" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-skill-state-4eba9d90" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dda177944e00eb4a">Why not rely on the model to recall current progress from all chat history in a long task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askill-state">SKILL.state: Scalable Long-Horizon Agent Skills</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>History grows and contains many failed attempts. Continuation needs clear completed work, unmet requirements, and key resources. SKILL.state maintains them as constrained execution state so new actions use current facts instead of reconstructing the whole past. The schema must be expressive enough.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: After changing three files, one failing test remains. The next turn should see that explicit item instead of guessing from dozens of messages.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26263">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.26263-skill-state/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dda177944e00eb4a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skill-state" data-paper-title="SKILL.state: Scalable Long-Horizon Agent Skills" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-cfd225f5bb30fb38">Why isn&#x27;t SKILL.state the full conversation with an extra state block?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askill-state">SKILL.state: Scalable Long-Horizon Agent Skills</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The next step receives only skill instructions, current state, and latest observation. Older conversation is not replayed, so persistent information must be written explicitly. Recursive patches preserve untouched fields and allow deletion; validation precedes commit. Full history would bypass state sufficiency and the capacity constraint.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Save a previously confirmed file path in state to use it next turn. Secretly keeping the full chat would not test whether state suffices.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26263">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.26263-skill-state/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cfd225f5bb30fb38">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skill-state" data-paper-title="SKILL.state: Scalable Long-Horizon Agent Skills" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-274f24591f4571fd">How does a fixed-schema state update differ from a generic rolling summary?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askill-state">SKILL.state: Scalable Long-Horizon Agent Skills</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Recursive patches preserve untouched fields and use null for explicit deletion. The runtime can check field names and types. Natural-language summaries are flexible but harder to constrain for overwrite and deletion. Valid structure does not guarantee factual contents or correct model updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A patch changing progress must preserve order_id. A prose rewrite may lose that ID without a clear field-level rejection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26263">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.26263-skill-state/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-274f24591f4571fd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skill-state" data-paper-title="SKILL.state: Scalable Long-Horizon Agent Skills" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f3d7aef13f674cc1">If action execution fails after valid state is committed, does the runtime undo state and external side effects?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askill-state">SKILL.state: Scalable Long-Horizon Agent Skills</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The paper commits valid state before the action. A local executor error does not trigger blind retry or imply external rollback. The caller must process the failure as latest observation. Format-retry and character caps are local safeguards; counter events do not prove a real LLM can generate correct patches.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: After recording a payment attempt, a network timeout does not justify resending it. Check the actual outcome to avoid double payment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 成本与复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26263">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.26263-skill-state/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f3d7aef13f674cc1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:caskg" data-paper-title="CaSKG: Counterfactual-Causal Skill Graphs for Scalable Agent Skill Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-caskg-e0c69536" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f00340222eb367d2">Why are several similar skills insufficient for an executable plan when the library grows?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acaskg">CaSKG: Counterfactual-Causal Skill Graphs for Scalable Agent Skill Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Jilin University / Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Skills can have order, input/output, and substitution relations. Similar wording does not make them compose. CaSKG retrieves skills together with reliable relations to avoid related but incompatible candidates. Calibration is needed beyond text similarity to claim dependency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Both lookup and modification relate to orders, but modification may require confirming payment first. Omitting that relationship can cause a bad sequence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25500">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.25500-caskg/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f00340222eb367d2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:caskg" data-paper-title="CaSKG: Counterfactual-Causal Skill Graphs for Scalable Agent Skill Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7ef6f17d03610eb0">Why calibrate semantic and I/O similarity edges with remove, substitute, and reorder probes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acaskg">CaSKG: Counterfactual-Causal Skill Graphs for Scalable Agent Skill Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Jilin University / Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similarity helps recall but does not prove a dependency or order. Text counterfactuals alter local structure to see whether the relation still holds; smoothing retains more reliable edges. This is evidence under the probes, not a verified causal effect in a real environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two skills mention uploading files, but removing authentication exposes a prerequisite. Shared vocabulary alone does not make them interchangeable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25500">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.25500-caskg/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7ef6f17d03610eb0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:caskg" data-paper-title="CaSKG: Counterfactual-Causal Skill Graphs for Scalable Agent Skill Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d742c44657a118f8">How does evidence from text counterfactual probes differ from real environmental interventions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acaskg">CaSKG: Counterfactual-Causal Skill Graphs for Scalable Agent Skill Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Jilin University / Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Text probes edit skill descriptions or order to calibrate relations, but may reflect judgments about wording. Real execution must verify action consequences and state. A causal name does not turn textual edge reliability into unconfounded causal evidence; distinguish mechanisms from capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A model predicts deletion of a step causes failure, but another tool may fill the same role. Test execution rather than rely on the prediction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25500">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.25500-caskg/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d742c44657a118f8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:caskg" data-paper-title="CaSKG: Counterfactual-Causal Skill Graphs for Scalable Agent Skill Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d9c99d17e5d0f4b">What do s, n, and the prior contribute to Bayesian smoothing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acaskg">CaSKG: Counterfactual-Causal Skill Graphs for Scalable Agent Skill Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Jilin University / Ant Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The posterior edge score is (α0+s)/(α0+β0+n). Successes add support, probe count controls shrinkage, and the prior avoids small-sample extremes. Publish only edges above threshold. One success is not probability one, and isolated local ToolRoute is not the full paper environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: One probe success and a hundred successes are not equivalent once the prior and different evidence amounts are considered.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25500">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.25500-caskg/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d9c99d17e5d0f4b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skillforge" data-paper-title="SkillForge: Automated Skill Discovery and Refinement for Tool-Using Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-skillforge-0aa71f73" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-06b43e737dc5b20f">Why does SkillForge teach skill selection rather than merely supplying a catalog?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askillforge">SkillForge: Automated Skill Discovery and Refinement for Tool-Using Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AMAP, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Procedural knowledge does not guarantee selection at the right time. Skills can be ignored, misused, or mismatched to current state. SkillForge learns invocation with actions and improves contents from execution, focusing on cooperation between knowledge and policy rather than document count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A stored validate-before-import skill does not help an agent that always imports directly. Task feedback must affect selection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24747">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.24747-skillforge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-06b43e737dc5b20f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skillforge" data-paper-title="SkillForge: Automated Skill Discovery and Refinement for Tool-Using Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a921645b2a022efd">Why activate, revise, or deduplicate skill candidates instead of appending every success permanently?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askillforge">SkillForge: Automated Skill Discovery and Refinement for Tool-Using Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AMAP, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One success may depend on incidental conditions. Old skills can go stale or conflict. Multi-path induction proposes candidates, then policy choices and environmental feedback determine use and revisions. Appending expands the library without ensuring fit and can reinforce bad retrievals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A download skill hard-codes an old button. If it fails in a new UI, revise or deactivate it instead of stacking another similar document.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24747">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.24747-skillforge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a921645b2a022efd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skillforge" data-paper-title="SkillForge: Automated Skill Discovery and Refinement for Tool-Using Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f88f7b4c307b67d5">How does multi-path induction from success, failure, and contrasts differ from summarizing successes only?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askillforge">SkillForge: Automated Skill Discovery and Refinement for Tool-Using Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AMAP, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Success supplies usable steps, failure exposes boundaries, and contrast helps identify meaningful differences. Candidates need not repeat one success, but remain hypotheses until environment validation. Do not convert guesses in failure narratives into reliable rules or generalize from one successful case.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Both trajectories use the same query, but only the successful one verifies results. Propose verification as important and test it rather than immediately claim causality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24747">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.24747-skillforge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f88f7b4c307b67d5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:skillforge" data-paper-title="SkillForge: Automated Skill Discovery and Refinement for Tool-Using Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-06647be6cbb7bceb">What must the local check record for a_t=(environment action, skill choice)?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Askillforge">SkillForge: Automated Skill Discovery and Refinement for Tool-Using Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · AMAP, Alibaba Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Record the skill selected by the policy at action time and its execution outcome; a post-hoc label is not enough. Local structured plans verify invocation, posterior, and revision control flow without LLM teacher induction or RL. Reuse counts are not a learned policy or paper environment score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Selecting a similar skill after an action to explain it is not actual use. Selection must influence action generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24747">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.24747-skillforge/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-06647be6cbb7bceb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hymem" data-paper-title="HyMem: Hierarchical Context Management for Long-Horizon Agents via Information Isolation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-hymem-ebf0c9bb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6f117905da9d1b3c">Why can a multi-stage task leak irrelevant details into global decisions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahymem">HyMem: Hierarchical Context Management for Long-Horizon Agents via Information Isolation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Search, execution, and reasoning create many artifacts. Sending all of them to one context lets old logs or tentative assumptions distract planning. HyMem gives each stage the information it needs and uses progress records to continue, moving necessary evidence rather than sharing every token.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Hundreds of compiler lines may help the repair worker; global planning may need only the cause and affected module.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15703">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.15703-hymem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6f117905da9d1b3c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hymem" data-paper-title="HyMem: Hierarchical Context Management for Long-Horizon Agents via Information Isolation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-79c1cf512c450ba6">Why can separating planning, execution, and isolated reasoning reduce context pollution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahymem">HyMem: Hierarchical Context Management for Long-Horizon Agents via Information Isolation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The layers need different detail: planning needs goal progress, execution needs current actions, and transient reasoning need not persist. Structured summaries retain necessary state across refreshes without crowding long-term facts with guesses. Isolation does not guarantee correctness; summaries must preserve constraints and provenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Pass verified interface changes and open issues from debugging to planning, not every tentative hypothesis as a lasting fact.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15703">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.15703-hymem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-79c1cf512c450ba6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hymem" data-paper-title="HyMem: Hierarchical Context Management for Long-Horizon Agents via Information Isolation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6af66bb3ebb4bbd4">What do structured progress summaries versus raw execution logs retain during handoff?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahymem">HyMem: Hierarchical Context Management for Long-Horizon Agents via Information Isolation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Raw logs retain detail and many local attempts, leaving the next layer to identify what matters. Structured progress extracts completed work, current state, and open items, giving planning a stable starting point. Compression can omit constraints, so test whether the handoff supports continuation rather than counting text reduction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Summarize installation logs as dependencies installed, tests not run due to missing credentials. &#x27;Install succeeded&#x27; alone may be mistaken for completed verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15703">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.15703-hymem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6af66bb3ebb4bbd4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hymem" data-paper-title="HyMem: Hierarchical Context Management for Long-Horizon Agents via Information Isolation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e300338bfd858cc0">Do deterministic local PlanBench results show that GAIA or BrowseComp-plus ran?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahymem">HyMem: Hierarchical Context Management for Long-Horizon Agents via Information Isolation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Local tests cover layered context, refresh summaries, and mechanism counts without browsers, external tools, or the paper&#x27;s large model. Cost units and saturated scores belong to the controlled protocol, not real long-horizon token costs or paper Pass@1.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Counting a summary as one fixture event does not show that a real web evidence summary preserves the same facts at the same cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15703">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.15703-hymem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e300338bfd858cc0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:vag" data-paper-title="When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-vag-dfb74800" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b7cc4ccf17a5ebda">Why is admitting experience a risky step for a self-evolving skill library?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avag">When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Candidate experience influences later actions and can be abstracted into new skills. One bad suggestion can therefore harm more than the current task. VaG limits this propagation so continual learning does not gradually corrupt long-term memory. Write volume does not measure progress.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A temporary check bypass gets generalized into a rule and reused across tasks. A short-term success becomes long-term contamination.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05810">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.05810-vag/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b7cc4ccf17a5ebda">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:vag" data-paper-title="When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-203b6b4073c19e5f">Why can&#x27;t deleting harmful skills after writing fully replace pre-admission validation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avag">When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A skill can influence new trajectories and descendant skills, spreading corruption before removal. Deleting its original entry does not undo derivatives. Precommit checks structure, behavioral harmlessness, and semantic consistency before choosing a compatible set. Admission and runtime rollback are distinct. Good individual skills may conflict together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An incorrect retry rule has been absorbed into another skill. Removing the original does not repair its descendant; validate before writing to reduce inherited corruption.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05810">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.05810-vag/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-203b6b4073c19e5f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:vag" data-paper-title="When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-28954ff9e44b5448">Why keep separate structural, behavioral harmlessness, and semantic consistency gates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avag">When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Structure checks parsability and references, behavior checks whether known executions regress, and semantics checks intended meaning. Valid formatting can hide bad actions, and one harmless run can miss unsafe preconditions. The gates supply complementary evidence but remain limited by case coverage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A perfectly formatted skill reverses &#x27;back up, then edit.&#x27; Parsing passes it, but semantic or behavioral validation can detect the reversal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05810">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.05810-vag/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-28954ff9e44b5448">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:vag" data-paper-title="When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-341ae6021330275f">Why not combine all individually high-scoring skills in the Hot set?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avag">When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Skills can conflict or duplicate, so set utility depends on shared context. VaG selects compatible combinations by marginal gain, not the sum of independent scores. Local tests cover gates and selection, not an expensive judge or original environment. Registering discovery does not prove a promotable real controller is integrated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: One skill requires caching first; another clears cache every step. Each can work alone, yet loading both requires a compatibility check.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05810">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.05810-vag/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-341ae6021330275f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gse" data-paper-title="Learning Globally Reusable Skills for Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-gse-c467dca4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a0059fed14785844">Why does GSE need a Skill Relation Graph for globally reusable skills?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agse">Learning Globally Reusable Skills for Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local experiences may overlap, complement, or conflict. The graph supports clustering and merges that avoid many near duplicates. Relationships still need evidence: semantic similarity does not make merging safe, especially when abstraction can erase environmental preconditions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Both tasks run tests, but one first generates configuration and the other already has it. Preserve the difference when merging.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06153">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.06153-gse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a0059fed14785844">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gse" data-paper-title="Learning Globally Reusable Skills for Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-08e42839803cd827">Why run replay verification after clustering and merging similar local skills?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agse">Learning Globally Reusable Skills for Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Similar wording can hide different preconditions, and merging can remove a branch critical to some tasks. Replay checks whether global reuse sacrifices old behavior, while the relation graph manages conflicts. Compact clusters and new successes do not independently establish safe merges or cross-distribution transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Merge parsers for files with and without headers, then replay both cases so the unified flow does not keep only one assumption.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06153">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.06153-gse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-08e42839803cd827">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gse" data-paper-title="Learning Globally Reusable Skills for Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a4e90ad057a46e13">How does global skill integration change the library differently from appending each task&#x27;s experience independently?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agse">Learning Globally Reusable Skills for Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Appending preserves local detail but accumulates similar, condition-specific, or conflicting skills. Integration uses relations to build reusable abstractions. It is not mere text deduplication: retain preconditions and validate old behavior. A smaller library or denser relations do not establish better execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two export tasks save files, but one requires encryption and the other publication. Preserve those conditions rather than merge them into publish everything.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06153">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.06153-gse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a4e90ad057a46e13">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:gse" data-paper-title="Learning Globally Reusable Skills for Coding Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a3a2c16881999ef1">Do local relation-graph and regression-penalty tests reproduce industrial Agent F1?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agse">Learning Globally Reusable Skills for Coding Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tianjin University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The public mini-suite executes graph, selection, and regression operators without the paper&#x27;s large model, private industrial environment, or expensive judge. Industrial F1 is full author-system evidence, not a consequence of smaller graphs or fixture scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Merging ten skills into five shows the merge happened. Without industrial test-generation tasks, it cannot imply precision or recall.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06153">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.06153-gse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a3a2c16881999ef1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memorycpt" data-paper-title="MemoryCPT: An End-to-End Agent Memory Framework for Cost-Performance Trade-off" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-memorycpt-45f8aee7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8ddb0c3f29f9f1b1">Why account separately for memory-writing and memory-use costs in long-lived assistants?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemorycpt">MemoryCPT: An End-to-End Agent Memory Framework for Cost-Performance Trade-off</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hong Kong University of Science and Technology / Tencent LIGHTSPEED STUDIOS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>History is written continually, while repeated queries trigger retrieval and summaries. Frequencies and cost drivers differ. MemoryCPT studies the end-to-end trade-off, making construction cheaper and reads question-specific. Shortening one summary does not establish system efficiency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Hundreds of daily writes and five reads make different bottlenecks than five writes and hundreds of reads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04843">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.04843-memorycpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8ddb0c3f29f9f1b1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memorycpt" data-paper-title="MemoryCPT: An End-to-End Agent Memory Framework for Cost-Performance Trade-off" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e2c6e5282ef27147">Why does Quality per Cost require more than shortening a query summary?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemorycpt">MemoryCPT: An End-to-End Agent Memory Framework for Cost-Performance Trade-off</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hong Kong University of Science and Technology / Tencent LIGHTSPEED STUDIOS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cost savings can harm answer quality, so the ratio may not improve. Construction, retrieval, and summarization each have inference costs. Offline chain distillation reduces construction, RRF and query-focused summaries manage reads, and cost-aware reward judges the pipeline. Compare the same quality definition rather than call fewer tokens success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Reducing 500 words to twenty may omit a crucial exception and cause a wrong answer. Eighty useful words may offer a better quality-cost trade-off.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04843">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.04843-memorycpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e2c6e5282ef27147">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memorycpt" data-paper-title="MemoryCPT: An End-to-End Agent Memory Framework for Cost-Performance Trade-off" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c04a3362054db9b8">Why optimize construction cost and per-query cost separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemorycpt">MemoryCPT: An End-to-End Agent Memory Framework for Cost-Performance Trade-off</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hong Kong University of Science and Technology / Tencent LIGHTSPEED STUDIOS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Construction processes incoming history, and reads recur with queries. They have different frequencies and useful information. MemoryCPT distills offline chains for construction and applies rank fusion and query-related summaries for reads. Sum actual write and query frequencies and check answer quality before claiming total savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Thousands of turns written but two queries can make construction dominate. Hundreds of reads from one history can compound small per-read savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04843">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.04843-memorycpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c04a3362054db9b8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memorycpt" data-paper-title="MemoryCPT: An End-to-End Agent Memory Framework for Cost-Performance Trade-off" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-acc6e61b27c2664b">Can text concatenation stand in for RRF retrieval and a LoRA summarizer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemorycpt">MemoryCPT: An End-to-End Agent Memory Framework for Cost-Performance Trade-off</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Hong Kong University of Science and Technology / Tencent LIGHTSPEED STUDIOS</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. RRF actually fuses rankings, the summarizer generates query-relevant context, and cost-aware GRPO needs real rewards and updates. Local tests retain core selection or state diagnostics without paper-scale training or benchmarks. Interface fields are not completed distillation or RL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Concatenating two ranked lists performs neither reciprocal rank fusion nor learned summarization. Supplying the text to a model does not mean QAR ran.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04843">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.04843-memorycpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-acc6e61b27c2664b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:vermem" data-paper-title="VerMem" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-vermem-8bc3a085" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-de819e9cc69de79c">Why manage long-term memory, active context, and episodic history together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avermem">VerMem</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sun Yat-sen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They jointly decide where information lives and what is visible. Separate optimization can misalign writing, restoring, and reading. VerMem selects atomic operations with one policy and verifies transitions locally and evidence globally. A shared policy does not make the state types interchangeable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A fact in long-term memory needs retrieve or restore before answering. Merely existing in history does not make it visible.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03137">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.03137-vermem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-de819e9cc69de79c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:vermem" data-paper-title="VerMem" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b3def5f3a30eb45a">Why check memory actions with separate local and global verifiers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avermem">VerMem</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sun Yat-sen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local checks validate one transition contract but cannot judge consistency across a long trajectory. Global verification checks the relationship between the whole trace and final memory. Both complement task reward so legal individual steps cannot quietly accumulate into false state. Verifier pass rate is not task accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Deleting a field may be locally valid but remove the only evidence for a later answer. Global evidence consistency should catch that.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03137">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.03137-vermem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b3def5f3a30eb45a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:vermem" data-paper-title="VerMem" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c058bd626ac200eb">Why do final task reward and memory-operation checks supervise different things?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avermem">VerMem</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sun Yat-sen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final reward measures the overall result but cannot locate a retrieval, storage, or restore fault. Verification checks transitions and evidence, while operation cost controls resource use. Success can contain illegal or wasteful steps, and legal steps can fail to solve the task. Keep the signals distinct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A lucky correct answer does not justify deleting key evidence. A legal retrieval need not find the answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03137">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.03137-vermem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c058bd626ac200eb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:vermem" data-paper-title="VerMem" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0c718fe823cf49a9">Does nonzero local operation telemetry reproduce all seven operations and full RL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avermem">VerMem</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Sun Yat-sen University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The README says the local run maintains three states and executes core retrieve, add, restore, and related paths. Counts prove those branches ran, not original multi-GPU RL or full environments. Claims must follow actual operations and budgets, not method names or counts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A positive restore count means recovery was invoked, not that a learned policy picks the right time on real long tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03137">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.03137-vermem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0c718fe823cf49a9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coevo-mem" data-paper-title="CoEvo-Mem" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-coevo-mem-e947b4e5" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d970af4f29aa476e">Why do routing policy and memory-bank updates affect each other?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoevo-mem">CoEvo-Mem</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Routing determines which memories are used; outcomes update route and memory utility. Content and graph changes then change route value. Optimizing one side alone can preserve the other&#x27;s defects. CoEvo-Mem alternates updates and learns only from actual trajectories, not invented results for untried routes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A route keeps selecting stale records. Changing the bank alters its payoff; after the update, routing must learn which paths work.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01739">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.01739-coevo-mem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d970af4f29aa476e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coevo-mem" data-paper-title="CoEvo-Mem" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f09a664c62c12948">Why alternate freezing the router and memory bank rather than updating both freely each round?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoevo-mem">CoEvo-Mem</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Routing changes which memories are seen; bank changes alter router feedback. If both drift together, effects are hard to attribute. Freeze one while updating the other to limit nonstationarity, and use a lightweight residual to preserve the base LLM prior. This makes feedback easier to learn and audit without guaranteeing convergence or gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Freeze memory to compare routes, then freeze routing to revise low-value entries. Changing both at once makes a failure hard to locate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01739">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.01739-coevo-mem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f09a664c62c12948">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:coevo-mem" data-paper-title="CoEvo-Mem" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3b67e8e3d352fecb">What are the roles of the frozen LLM&#x27;s routing prior and the trainable residual router?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Acoevo-mem">CoEvo-Mem</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The base LLM contributes task understanding as a routing prior. A residual changes selection using real interaction feedback without retraining the full model.
