<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memtool" data-paper-title="MemTool" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-13511d15aa68dae4">How do autonomous, workflow, and hybrid tool-description policies make decisions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemtool">MemTool</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · PricewaterhouseCoopers Commercial Technology and Innovation Office</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Autonomous lets the agent decide retention; workflow uses current process requirements; hybrid protects those requirements and dynamically manages remaining tools. Freedom and structural constraints differ. Removal rate is insufficient if eviction prevents completion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An agent may discard rare payments before one is needed. Workflow information protects payment while hybrid manages other entries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与算法. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21428">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2507.21428-memtool/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-13511d15aa68dae4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memtool" data-paper-title="MemTool" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c38703d1cf219e1f">How should recency and historical success scores evict unprotected tools?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemtool">MemTool</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · PricewaterhouseCoopers Commercial Technology and Innovation Office</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Restrict candidates to those outside the protected workflow set. Keep scores λ times recency plus (1−λ) times success; evict the lowest. The weight trades off recency and history without redefining protection. Local deterministic descriptions and eviction counts do not establish live tool completion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: One evictable tool was just used but often fails; another is older but reliable. λ controls the choice, and required tools do not enter this ranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与算法, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21428">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2507.21428-memtool/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c38703d1cf219e1f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memgpt" data-paper-title="MemGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-memgpt-81032c11" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-21988cc15fb83697">Why does MemGPT compare long documents and conversations to limited-memory management?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemgpt">MemGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One context window is finite while user material can be much larger. MemGPT lets agents schedule information across visible working memory and external storage to continue long tasks. Archive capacity does not imply current knowledge; finding, paging, and storing information affect answers and cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: To answer about a six-month-old contract, locate and page in the relevant record. Having the file on disk is not enough.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08560">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2310.08560-memgpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-21988cc15fb83697">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memgpt" data-paper-title="MemGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-aaf7b125e9d02507">Why actively manage page-in and page-out when the external archive is large?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemgpt">MemGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Archive capacity is not visible context. Relevant material must enter the working window to affect an answer. Paging links storage to the current task, and heartbeats or interrupts schedule further evidence gathering and user interaction. A virtual-memory interface does not let a model see unlimited history at once.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An old address remains in the archive. Retrieve and page it in before answering a shipping question.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08560">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2310.08560-memgpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aaf7b125e9d02507">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memgpt" data-paper-title="MemGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ae4e9dea4029ce9d">How does a heartbeat differ from a normal user-facing response in control flow?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemgpt">MemGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Heartbeat or interrupt continues internal memory and tool work rather than treating each operation as a final response. This is a scheduling interface, not a guarantee of correct invocation. Unconditional loops can waste budget, so use it only for relevant pending work.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: After paging old content out, continue internal retrieval and answer once relevant evidence is loaded instead of returning a partial status as the answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08560">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2310.08560-memgpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ae4e9dea4029ce9d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:memgpt" data-paper-title="MemGPT" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-656d6a06d31b8c18">Does deterministic key-based page-in establish semantic archive retrieval?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Amemgpt">MemGPT</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Local tests cover hierarchical state, paging, and interrupt counts, using deterministic keys instead of embeddings or LLM function calls. Proxy cost is not token count or latency. Paging works, but real autonomous evidence retrieval from long documents is unverified.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Getting an entry by order123 is easier than understanding and retrieving the user&#x27;s vaguely mentioned last order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08560">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2310.08560-memgpt/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-656d6a06d31b8c18">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:voyager" data-paper-title="Voyager" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-voyager-f3989bf0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-fc830cd6a7e32dd0">Why does Voyager use code as an action instead of only a natural-language plan?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avoyager">Voyager</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Code invokes environment APIs over extended behavior and can be iteratively repaired from errors and observations. Successful programs enter the library for reuse. Natural-language plans still need executable mapping. Runnable code can also be wrong and needs environmental validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Compile collecting wood into movement, search, and harvesting loops, then inspect inventory. Saying &#x27;chop a tree&#x27; does not perform those actions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2305.16291-voyager/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fc830cd6a7e32dd0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:voyager" data-paper-title="Voyager" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-aa9ceda6b2719950">Why admit only programs verified by the environment to Voyager&#x27;s skill library?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avoyager">Voyager</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Plausible code can fail because materials are missing, APIs are wrong, or goals are unmet. Environment feedback exposes these failures. Index confirmed successes for reuse. The automatic curriculum picks new goals and the library retains verified behavior; code generation alone cannot substitute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A program for crafting an iron pickaxe is not a successful skill if inventory lacks iron. Only actual completion supports future reuse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2305.16291-voyager/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aa9ceda6b2719950">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:voyager" data-paper-title="Voyager" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e1d7d24beac16b9f">How does automatic curriculum differ from a fixed checklist for accumulating skills?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avoyager">Voyager</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The curriculum chooses novel goals from current state and skills. A fixed list is controlled but cannot adapt to capability. Self-selected goals can favor easy novelty, so validate outcomes and progress rather than treat task count or exploration distance as general capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: After acquiring stone tools, mining explores more than repeated wood gathering, but completion still depends on inventory and milestones.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2305.16291-voyager/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e1d7d24beac16b9f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:voyager" data-paper-title="Voyager" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cf860a830a3dce6b">Is the local structured-plan skill library equivalent to Mineflayer JavaScript programs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Avoyager">Voyager</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Curriculum, skills, verification, and cross-episode reuse are retained with structured tool plans. The run omits Minecraft, GPT-4, and embedding retrieval. Controlled retry counts do not represent real program debugging or paper item and distance gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Reusing a plan template does not show handling Mineflayer&#x27;s asynchronous movement errors or achieving its technology-tree gains in a new world.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16291">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2305.16291-voyager/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cf860a830a3dce6b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:generative-agents" data-paper-title="Generative Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-generative-agents-beb05f66" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f33684b6de1a3530">How does reflection differ from recording a single observation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agenerative-agents">Generative Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Observations are concrete events. Reflection draws higher-level inferences across important memories for retrieval and planning. Inferences can be wrong and are not primary evidence. Keep observations traceable and plans grounded in current state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Several helpful acts may suggest someone is cooperative. That is an abstraction, not a new observed event, and should retain support.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03442">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2304.03442-generative-agents/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f33684b6de1a3530">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:generative-agents" data-paper-title="Generative Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c25df77a18e7bbd">Why shouldn&#x27;t an important old event automatically replace more query-relevant memory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agenerative-agents">Generative Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Importance captures long-term significance, relevance measures current fit, and recency models decay. Reflection abstracts several important events, but actions still need current state. Using one dimension alone can repeat major events or focus only on recent chatter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Moving home was important, but last night&#x27;s restaurant confirmation better answers today&#x27;s dinner-location question.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03442">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2304.03442-generative-agents/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c25df77a18e7bbd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:generative-agents" data-paper-title="Generative Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-86aad2b622fd5b5f">What questions do reflection and planning answer in everyday behavior simulation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agenerative-agents">Generative Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reflection forms higher-level interpretations from experiences, such as relationship or habit inferences. Planning schedules what to do next using goals, memory, and time. Inferences are not events, and plans are not executed results. Separation makes both evidence and actual behavior traceable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Inferring that a neighbor likes gardening is reflection. Deciding to invite them to buy seeds this afternoon is planning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03442">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2304.03442-generative-agents/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-86aad2b622fd5b5f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:generative-agents" data-paper-title="Generative Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-77326fa7f7760be0">Do local reflection triggers include a social evaluation of 25 LLM personas?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Agenerative-agents">Generative Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Controlled EvoMem tests three-score retrieval, cumulative-importance triggers, and planning dependencies without a Smallville map, real personas, or human credibility judgments. Reflection counts and proxy costs show mechanism execution, not believable relationships or coordination.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A threshold producing one rule-based reflection does not show models spreading invitations or arranging a party.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03442">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2304.03442-generative-agents/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-77326fa7f7760be0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:discernmem" data-paper-title="Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-discernmem-43739873" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-208331253abf4012">Why not rewrite every memory used after a team failure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adiscernmem">Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-29 · East China Normal University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Another role, a tool or an out-of-scope scenario may have caused the failure. DiscernMem compares replay with just the suspect memory against no-memory replay on the same task, seed and configuration. It then asks whether the rule body is defective or a useful rule was used out of scope. A negative effect alone does not prove a defective body.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Repair the source before running tests may help with code bugs. If the test environment is broken, more source edits can harm. Add an avoid scope rather than delete a useful source-repair rule.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36652v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.36652-discernmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-208331253abf4012">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:discernmem" data-paper-title="Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-79284be821911bd5">Why compare a proposed repair to both its parent memory and a no-memory baseline?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adiscernmem">Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-29 · East China Normal University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The parent may already be harmful. Merely beating it can still underperform injecting nothing. For each task in the fixed trigger and history sets, the proposal must match the better reference minus tolerance, without adding outright failures. This protects tested behavior, not every unseen task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Parent 0.2, no memory 0.8, proposal 0.7. The proposal beats its parent by 0.5 but misses the 0.79 threshold with default tolerance 0.01; reject it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36652v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.36652-discernmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-79284be821911bd5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:discernmem" data-paper-title="Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ceac2d055153b0af">How does testing only on the triggering failure differ from DiscernMem&#x27;s cross-task validation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adiscernmem">Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-29 · East China Normal University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A local fix can harm past capabilities. DiscernMem fixes a set of triggers, previous positive-effect tasks and related tasks, then applies thresholds per task, not to the mean. Related tasks must not regress; they need not improve. Origin tasks are excluded from history validation so the original example cannot repeatedly validate its own memory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Trigger improves 0.4→0.9 and an old task drops 0.8→0.5. Reject even though the mean improves.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与实现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36652v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.36652-discernmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ceac2d055153b0af">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:discernmem" data-paper-title="Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3fc0461b8244cb89">Why can&#x27;t a new memory body inherit the parent&#x27;s success evidence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adiscernmem">Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-29 · East China Normal University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Effects are tied to the body actually used. The new body has not shown the same reliability. Keep identity, owner and compliant correction history, but clear previous effect evidence and mark the new version provisional. This versioning component is not evidence of LLM repair or multi-agent ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: v2 worked on ten tasks. If v3 adds a stopping condition, keep v2 records but start v3&#x27;s effects empty; do not say v3 passed the ten tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与实现边界, 本地结果与负控. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36652v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.36652-discernmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3fc0461b8244cb89">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:emma" data-paper-title="EMMA: Structured Episodic Memory for Multi-Agent Workflow Synthesis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-emma-e2de2da1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b5bc65c5db3ad6e9">Why doesn&#x27;t EMMA turn every failure into a new skill?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aemma">EMMA: Structured Episodic Memory for Multi-Agent Workflow Synthesis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · University of California San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ownership depends on the error. Use task-local plan guidance for one execution slip, agent prompts for general habits, skills for missing procedures and controller changes for routing. Experience at the wrong scope can fail to trigger or interfere elsewhere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Checking units can be reusable. One misclick does not require a permanent unit-check skill or a new agent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35966v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.35966-emma/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b5bc65c5db3ad6e9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:emma" data-paper-title="EMMA: Structured Episodic Memory for Multi-Agent Workflow Synthesis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c81e84114c9000a3">Why require one edited entry and retain at least 60% of old prompt lines?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aemma">EMMA: Structured Episodic Memory for Multi-Agent Workflow Synthesis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · University of California San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Single-entry and ownership scope bound location; retention, length and pool capacity bound magnitude. Only agents involved in the failed attempt may change. New entries must actually be used in the next plan. Structural validity is not better task performance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Keeping two of five lines and replacing the role is rejected. Keeping three and adding a local check reaches 60%, but still needs an external rerun.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地结果与负控. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35966v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.35966-emma/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c81e84114c9000a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:emma" data-paper-title="EMMA: Structured Episodic Memory for Multi-Agent Workflow Synthesis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-628c21208d8098ea">Why treat context overflow differently from missing capability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aemma">EMMA: Structured Episodic Memory for Multi-Agent Workflow Synthesis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · University of California San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Overflow can mean a step is too broad. Split incomplete steps and resume without discarding finished work. A new specialist needs evidence of missing capability or repeated overflow; repeated overflow calls for changing the decomposition, not simply changing prompts/skills.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If steps one and two already produced a table and step three is too large, keep the table and subdivide step three among existing agents.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式, 代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35966v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.35966-emma/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-628c21208d8098ea">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:emma" data-paper-title="EMMA: Structured Episodic Memory for Multi-Agent Workflow Synthesis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c89ecfb26059fd12">Do passing local guards prove no memory leakage and a stronger agent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aemma">EMMA: Structured Episodic Memory for Multi-Agent Workflow Synthesis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-30 · University of California San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The code checks ownership, capacity, retention, rotation, lifecycle and concatenation. Independent external services judge semantic deduplication, real specialization and leakage; the component cannot prove those judgments correct. No evaluated actor, LLM reflection or real task traces.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A service may incorrectly mark an answer-bearing proposal safe. A Boolean interface cannot detect that; local rejection counts are not AppWorld success rates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 数据协议与实现边界, 本地结果与负控, 高成本完整实验. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35966v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.35966-emma/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c89ecfb26059fd12">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:engram-consolidation" data-paper-title="ENGRAM: From Agent Experience to Weights through Verified Consolidation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-engram-consolidation-28eba53e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3bfe7db63e259653">Why can a skill enter ENGRAM training if the student has never completed it? Does admission immediately allow record removal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aengram-consolidation">ENGRAM: From Agent Experience to Weights through Verified Consolidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-09 · University of New South Wales</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Enough successful teacher demonstrations can admit a skill on their own. Admission only authorizes an attempt to learn. Without a valid current training contribution and reserved verification probes, the records cannot be released.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: At zero mastery, two successful records from one teacher episode satisfy d_min=2. If both are reserved as development probes, neither contributes to the current training batch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09472">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2611.09472-engram-consolidation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3bfe7db63e259653">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:engram-consolidation" data-paper-title="ENGRAM: From Agent Experience to Weights through Verified Consolidation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4c100ec81c202a20">Why require both a relative margin and a strict absolute floor?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aengram-consolidation">ENGRAM: From Agent Experience to Weights through Verified Consolidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-09 · University of New South Wales</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The relative margin bounds the tolerated decline when weights replace retrieval. The absolute floor prevents a small improvement from passing when both arms perform poorly. Equality at the relative margin passes; equality at the absolute floor fails.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: The candidate gets two of four probes right and the reference gets one. At a margin of 0.25 and a floor of 0.5, the relative condition passes, but the floor prevents release.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 原文效果与负结果. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09472">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2611.09472-engram-consolidation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4c100ec81c202a20">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:engram-consolidation" data-paper-title="ENGRAM: From Agent Experience to Weights through Verified Consolidation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d9a50f0bc981a580">If MemPrice omits a memory&#x27;s raw text, is that equivalent to ENGRAM releasing records for the skill?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aengram-consolidation">ENGRAM: From Agent Experience to Weights through Verified Consolidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-09 · University of New South Wales</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. MemPrice selects a representation for the current window, or omits the item, using utility and budget. ENGRAM uses a base model with retrieval as the reference and requires the updated weights to pass independent probes before records can move out of retrieval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: A short window may fit only keywords. That does not prove the model can perform the task without retrieval. Passing the release gate also does not erase the archived originals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 原文效果与负结果. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09472">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2611.09472-engram-consolidation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d9a50f0bc981a580">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:engram-consolidation" data-paper-title="ENGRAM: From Agent Experience to Weights through Verified Consolidation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/memory-and-skills">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Memory and skills: retrieval, reuse, and invalidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d04b1bd3531ede40">May two segments from the same source episode go into training and development separately if they have different skill labels?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aengram-consolidation">ENGRAM: From Agent Experience to Weights through Verified Consolidation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-09 · University of New South Wales</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Keep each originating episode in one split regardless of skill labels. Reserved episodes must not appear in training replay either. Only the independent grader sees the probe target. The paper&#x27;s pre-release reference retrieval store is a different concept from the training split.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: Navigation and checkout steps from one shopping attempt cannot straddle training and development. Turning off episodic retrieval should not hide the current checkout page.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09472">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2611.09472-engram-consolidation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d04b1bd3531ede40">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<details class="ar-learning-guide" markdown="1"><summary>Topic guide and reading order</summary>

## Start with this question

When history exceeds the context window, what should be saved, when should it be retrieved, and how can stale knowledge be kept from misleading a new task?

## Takeaway

Memory is state with write, retrieve, update, and eviction policies. MemGPT moves information between storage tiers so a limited window can access archives on demand. Voyager stores successful programs as retrievable skills. Facts, temporary inferences, and executable skills have different reuse conditions; facts can expire and a program may require a specific tool version. Start from the future decision and retain evidence for it. EMMA distinguishes one execution mistake, a persistent habit, a missing method, and misrouting before changing a plan, prompt, skill, or controller. Responsibility for repair matters as much as storage tier.

## Example

For a data project across sessions, keep confirmed unit conventions in resident memory, the current question and intermediate statistics in working memory, and complete queries and sources in the archive. When a table changes, verify schema before reusing query skills. Invalidate old units if the user changes them. Compressing everything to “prefers brevity” cannot recover calculation rules.

## Common pitfall

Readable summaries may still lose essential details. A retrieval hit may not apply. Evaluate task results, storage and call budgets, propagation of errors, and cross-user isolation. Local paging, skill lookup, or state fixtures do not establish real long-term memory or runs in original environments such as Minecraft.

## Reading order

Read MemGPT for moving information between context and archives, Voyager for executable skills versus facts, and Generative Agents for connecting retrieval, reflection, and planning without treating simulated social behavior as production evidence.

1. [MemGPT](../../../../agent-research/2310.08560-memgpt/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08560)
2. [Voyager](../../../../agent-research/2305.16291-voyager/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16291)
3. [Generative Agents](../../../../agent-research/2304.03442-generative-agents/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03442)

## Check your understanding

A skill once passed tests and has the highest retrieval score, but its tool interface just changed. Should the agent run it immediately?

??? note "Show suggested answer"

    First check interface version, input assumptions, and permissions, then run a cheap validation. Similarity does not establish present applicability. Track scope, feedback, and invalidation. If compatibility cannot be verified, use current evidence rather than trusting a historical pass.

</details>
